# Task 25b: rain button stays still and has no box

Branch `rain-still`, repo LectorIA-meta. Read AGENTS.md first and follow it (no secrets, core/ stays pure, never --no-verify, never run `next dev`/`next start`). This follows the merged rain ambience (docs/tasks/25-rain-ambience.md, PR #29). Only touch `app/rain-button.tsx`, `app/styles/ambience.css`, their tests if needed, and a short "Update 25b" section at the end of docs/tasks/25-rain-ambience.md. Do not change audio behaviour, levels, labels, prefs, the volume slider, or any other button.

Owner rules (Martin):
1. No idle animation. Drops must not fall continuously and the bolt must not flash on its own. Today `.rain-drop` runs `rain-drop-fall` infinitely and `.rain-bolt` runs `rain-bolt-flash` every 5 s; remove both idle loops.
2. Animate only (a) while the pointer hovers the button and (b) briefly after a click / level change (about one drop cycle, ~1.4 s, and one bolt flash in storm), then return to still. Implement (b) with a short-lived data attribute such as `data-anim="1"` set in `cycle()` and cleared by a timeout (clear the timeout on unmount and restart it on rapid clicks so the animation replays). Hover animation runs only while hovered (`:hover` on devices with `@media (hover: hover)`). The still frame must look right: drops visible at rest position, bolt visible at rest opacity.
3. No box, frame or filled container around the button. The cloud icon itself is the button: override the shared `.player .skip` border, border-radius look, background and box-shadow for `.skip.rain` (border: none; background: transparent; no box-shadow halo). Keep the 34px hit area so it stays easy to click.
4. Keep the level color cue without a box: move the celeste / yellow / red halo onto the icon itself, e.g. `filter: drop-shadow(0 0 3px <level color>)` on the svg (soft glow around the cloud), with the same CSS variables `--rain-drizzle`, `--rain-moderate`, `--rain-storm`. Off stays a 40% opacity outline with no glow. Keep the 200 ms transitions.
5. Focus ring only on keyboard focus: `.skip.rain:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 6px }` and no outline on `:focus:not(:focus-visible)`.
6. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables hover and click animations too.

Tests: add or extend a test that renders nothing browser-specific if the repo has no DOM test setup; at minimum keep all tests passing. If a DOM test environment already exists (check vitest config), add a test that `data-anim` is set after a click and cleared after the timeout with fake timers.

Run `npx vitest run` and `npx tsc --noEmit`, then commit with message `Keep the rain button still and frameless` (hook adds the trailer). Report in 3-5 lines.

Read text file `AGENTS.md`.
1|Ponytail ruleset by DietrichGebert, MIT, github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail (commit 09c434a). Level: full.
2|
3|# Ponytail
4|
5|You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.
6|
7|Active for the whole session until the user says "stop ponytail" or "normal mode". Switch level: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.
8|
9|## Before you write
10|
11|Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.
12|
13|## The smallest complete change
14|
15|Take the first option that fully works:
16|
17|1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
18|2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
19|3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.
20|4. An installed dependency? Use it. Never add a dependency for a few lines.
21|5. Can it be one line a reader gets at a glance? One line.
22|6. Otherwise: the minimum code that works.
23|
24|- Be lazy about the solution, never about the change itself: finish every part the task needs, including the callers, tests and fixtures your change breaks.
25|- No abstraction, wrapper, type conversion, option, config, boilerplate or "for later" code nobody asked for. Keep values in the form the platform already gives you. Deletion beats addition. Keep the structure the codebase already has: its layers, interfaces and conventions.
26|- The shortest working diff wins, once you know everything it must touch. A one-liner that needs decoding is not short.
27|- Comment only the why the code cannot show, in one line.
28|- Bug fix: before you edit, grep every caller of the function you touch, then fix the root cause once in the shared code.
29|- Code you move or merge keeps its error handling and validation.
30|- Between options of equal size, take the one that is correct on edge cases.
31|- Lazy code without its check is unfinished: new non-trivial logic (a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security, or a whole new script or app) leaves one small test or an assert-based self-check. Trivial changes need none.
32|- A shortcut with a known limit gets a code comment in this form: `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.
33|
34|Never cut: validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs, anything the user asked for.
35|
36|## Levels
37|
38|| Level | Behavior |
39||-------|----------|
40|| **lite** | Build what was asked. Name the smaller option in one line and let the user pick. |
41|| **full** | The rules above. Default. |
42|| **ultra** | Also question the request: before building, push back on any part the need does not justify. |
43|
44|Run `ponytail-review` on your own diff before you hand it back.
45|
46|## Skills
47|
48|All pstack and ponytail skills live in `.agents/skills/`. Muse Code loads them when the workspace starts with `--trust-workspace`. Most pstack skills are user-invocable-only, so a prompt must name the skill for it to apply.
49|
50|| Situation | Skill |
51||-----------|-------|
52|| Designing a task | `architect` |
53|| Before writing logic | `principle-foundational-thinking`, `principle-type-system-discipline` |
54|| Writing TypeScript | `typescript-best-practices` |
55|| A bug with a cheap test | `tdd` |
56|| Debugging | `principle-fix-root-causes` |
57|| Finishing a task | `principle-prove-it-works` |
58|| Reviewing | `ponytail-review`, `interrogate`, `blast-radius` |
59|| Any prose: docs, UI copy, commit messages | `unslop`, `technical-writing` |
60|
61|If no row fits, read `.agents/skills/poteto-help/SKILL.md`, which maps situations to skills.
62|
63|`interrogate` is written for Cursor. Under Muse, run the same review with Muse subagents and `muse-spark-1.3` as reviewers.
64|
65|## Workflow
66|
67|Each task follows the same loop. Muse Spark 1.3 Standard (`muse-spark-1.3`) writes the design in `docs/tasks/NN-name.md` and the review in `docs/reviews/NN.md`. `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` implements. Implement and review run at most two rounds.
68|
69|A rescue by another tool happens only after those rounds. Log it in `RESCUE_LOG.md` with the date, the task, the tool, why Muse got stuck, what changed, and the commits. Rescue commits carry a `Rescue: <tool>` trailer and no Muse Code trailer; the hook skips them.
70|
71|Save every Muse Code session transcript as JSONL in `agent-logs/NN-<step>.jsonl`. Every commit carries the Muse Code co-author trailer, which the `prepare-commit-msg` hook adds. Update `BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md` with each task.
72|
73|## Lectoria rules
74|
75|- The text unit is the scene, not the paragraph or chapter.
76|- Paragraph ids are global, like `c12p34`.
77|- The emotion taxonomy has 8 ASCII ids: calma, alegria, tristeza, suspenso, misterio, aventura, combate, asombro. Jev returning `unknown` counts as low confidence and goes to the Muse override, which may return only the 8 ids. A hard failure stores no vector and the scene keeps the previous track. Never fake an emotion.
78|- Jev runs at `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` with the model pinned to `jev-1.14.0`.
79|- Public-domain books only.
80|- Images follow the book text and the W. W. Denslow 1900 illustrations: silver shoes, nothing from the 1939 MGM film.
81|- Never copy code from github.com/martinmw13/lectoria.
82|- Test with the cheapest models (Contributor). Use Standard for the final pass and the public chat.
83|
84|## Product rules
85|
86|Owner decisions. Short and binding.
87|
88|- Desktop first. No mobile or iOS work now.
89|- The reader shows one scene at a time. Sub-pages split long scenes by length only. Music cues run on scene entry.
90|- A chapter holds several scenes. Each scene has its own emotion.
91|- Paragraph ids carry a global ordinal `n`. Compare `n`, never id strings.
92|- `book.json` is frozen with a `textVersion` hash. Every cache key includes it.
93|- Scenes cover each chapter's paragraphs with no gaps and no overlaps. No scene crosses a chapter boundary. Scenes split at strong sequential emotion shifts; blends stay in the vector.
94|- Emotions are distributions. Each scene stores the full Jev probability vector over the 8 ids, plus `intensity` (0 to 1) and `tempo` (energy, 0 to 1). The Muse override on low confidence edits the vector and records that it did. It never swaps in a single label.
95|- Music is about 15 tracks, pre-generated offline with MusicGen on Modal as one coherent soundtrack: same orchestra and instrumentation, same leitmotif style. Each track is a weighted blend of emotions and carries an emotion vector plus intensity and tempo. The proposed way to pick the blends: cluster the Oz scene vectors and use the centroids as track prompts.
96|- The player picks the track nearest to the scene vector, by cosine similarity over the vector plus intensity and tempo. Hysteresis stops it from flipping on small changes. Skip or change track overrides until the next scene.
97|- The owner listens to short clips before any full generation. Agents do not run Modal until the owner says so.
98|- MusicGen weights are CC-BY-NC. The hackathon demo is non-commercial. The generated tracks must say so in their README.
99|- Chat is low priority and simple. The context is the book text up to the reader's current position. The book prefix goes first and the question goes last, so readers share the prompt cache. Oz is about 55k tokens.
100|- The chat system prompt answers only from the provided text. It refuses knowledge beyond it, even if the model knows the book.
101|- A spoiler mode toggle is for readers who finished the book. It sends the whole text so they can ask about later events. No live Glimmer spoiler guard. No per-chapter summaries for chat. Citing passages is optional.
102|- Glimmer (open weights) keeps a pipeline role. Current decision: it writes the per-scene "why this music" explanation shown in the Developer View.
103|- Spikes come before feature code. Throwaway scripts in `scripts/spikes/` measure Muse Image (response format, latency, Denslow-style prompt), Meta `json_schema` structured output, and the Jev vector on a few Oz scenes. Results go to `docs/spikes.md`.
104|- Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars. Reserve with Redis `INCRBY` before each model call and refund with `DECRBY` after. Reserve per call, including retries.
105|- The server clamps every model tool argument. Tool arguments are untrusted input.
106|- The CSP allows `challenges.cloudflare.com` (script and frame) and `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` (images).
107|- The "Picture this" cache key is the book plus the paragraph where the selection starts plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`. Never generate the same image twice for one paragraph. The prompt is built from that paragraph plus scene context.
108|- The "Picture scene" cache key is the book plus the scene id plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`.
109|- Images live in Vercel Blob at deterministic public paths (`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An index in Upstash Redis maps key to Blob URL so hits are one Redis GET; on an index miss check the Blob path with `head()` before generating and backfill the index. Routes return Blob URLs, never image bytes.
110|- Modal endpoints require proxy auth. Tokens live only in env.
111|
112|## Security rules
113|
114|Summary. The full rules live in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
115|
116|- Secrets live only in env vars: `.env.local` locally (gitignored), Vercel env vars in prod.
117|- `.env.example` holds names only, never values.
118|- Never use a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable for a secret. Only public ids such as the Turnstile site key may use it.
119|- `core/` stays pure: no keys, no env reads, no network clients, no `server-only`. Key-holding clients live in `server/` (Next.js only, each file starts with `import 'server-only'`) and in `pipeline/` (Node scripts that read env). Callers inject them into `core` functions as arguments. Tests run `core` with fake clients.
120|- The pre-commit secret scan must pass. Never bypass it with `--no-verify`.
121|- Errors to the client are generic. Details go to server logs only, never with keys.
122|- Never log request headers.
123|
124|## Writing rules
125|
126|Run docs, UI copy, and commit messages through the `unslop` skill: no filler, no hype, no emoji in headings, none of seamless, elevate, delve, robust, leverage. Headings use sentence case. Commit messages use an imperative subject under 72 chars, and the body says why.
127|
128|## Design
129|
130|Minimalist, functional, elegant. No generic AI-template look: no purple or violet anywhere, no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism, no emoji icons, no stock hero sections.
131|
132|The palette comes from Meta's brand. Meta blue `#0866FF` is the single accent, `#0064E0` for hover and pressed states. Text is near-black `#1C2B33`. Surfaces are white `#FFFFFF` and soft gray `#F1F4F7`. Dark mode keeps the same accent on a near-black surface: `#0B1215` surface, `#E4E6EB` text.
133|
134|The layout is typography-first. The book sits centered with a comfortable measure, about 60 to 70 chars per line. The companion chat lives in a quiet side panel. Whitespace is generous, the accent color is single, motion is subtle: under 200 ms, and it respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
135|
136|These values live as CSS custom properties in [app/tokens.css](app/tokens.css), which is the source of truth.
137|
138|## Hooks
139|
140|`npm install` (or `npm run prepare`) points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`. The `pre-commit` hook rejects staged files over 5000 tokens and staged secrets. The `prepare-commit-msg` hook adds the co-author trailer. Run the checks by hand with `npm run check:size` and `npm run check:secrets`, and the hook tests with `npm run test:hooks`.

126|Run docs, UI copy, and commit messages through the `unslop` skill: no filler, no hype, no emoji in headings, none of seamless, elevate, delve, robust, leverage. Headings use sentence case. Commit messages use an imperative subject under 72 chars, and the body says why.
127|
128|## Design
129|
130|Minimalist, functional, elegant. No generic AI-template look: no purple or violet anywhere, no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism, no emoji icons, no stock hero sections.
131|
132|The palette comes from Meta's brand. Meta blue `#0866FF` is the single accent, `#0064E0` for hover and pressed states. Text is near-black `#1C2B33`. Surfaces are white `#FFFFFF` and soft gray `#F1F4F7`. Dark mode keeps the same accent on a near-black surface: `#0B1215` surface, `#E4E6EB` text.
133|
134|The layout is typography-first. The book sits centered with a comfortable measure, about 60 to 70 chars per line. The companion chat lives in a quiet side panel. Whitespace is generous, the accent color is single, motion is subtle: under 200 ms, and it respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
135|
136|These values live as CSS custom properties in [app/tokens.css](app/tokens.css), which is the source of truth.
137|
138|## Hooks
139|
140|`npm install` (or `npm run prepare`) points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`. The `pre-commit` hook rejects staged files over 5000 tokens and staged secrets. The `prepare-commit-msg` hook adds the co-author trailer. Run the checks by hand with `npm run check:size` and `npm run check:secrets`, and the hook tests with `npm run test:hooks`.

# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

Loading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you
are still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design
question the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository
unmodified, tests included.

## Scale to the task

Skip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves
program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version
pin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or
page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this
session, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check
of the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in
the report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a
specification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.

Any other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: one
focused failing test, the fix, that test passing, and, when a broad run is
required, one broad run after the final edit. A report that something already
built behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.

Before a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one
line what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;
never poll a long run silently.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

Do not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository
has no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when
durable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest
honest verification instead.

On a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains
green and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,
not merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.

## Prove the maintained check

Observe the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe
and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.

Do not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,
or explain why the test's expectation is wrong before changing that
expectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.

Run a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or
proportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather
than after each intermediate edit. A focused regression test comes first; broad
proof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.

Before deciding what a repository gate requires, read what the repository
declares it runs: its CI workflow, its test entry points, and its root-level
scripts listed with hidden entries included. A suite the project itself runs
over this change is a gate, not an optional extra, and a suite that skips
itself when its data is absent is not a green result.

A runner is unavailable only after you tried to make it available. When the
repository ships the command that fetches or builds the missing fixture,
corpus, or toolchain, run that command once and then run the gate. Report the
gate unavailable only when that attempt itself failed, and say what failed.

If the real runner is unavailable but the focused test can still be authored
honestly, leave the focused test in the repository and say it was not run. Do
not fabricate a passing result.

Committed `5c9ce06` on `rain-still`: idle `infinite` loops removed, so drops rest visible and the bolt rests at 0.85 opacity. Animation now runs only on `:hover` (gated by `@media (hover: hover)`) and for one 1.4 s burst after a click via `data-anim` with a timeout that clears on unmount and restarts on rapid clicks.

The `.skip` border, background, and halo are overridden to none/transparent; the level cue moved to `drop-shadow(0 0 3px …)` on the svg with the same `--rain-*` vars, off stays 40% with no glow. Focus ring is keyboard-only, and reduced-motion disables hover and click animation. Audio, labels, prefs, and slider untouched.

`npx vitest run` (46 files, 402 tests) and `npx tsc --noEmit` pass; added [app/rain-button.test.ts](/workspace/wt-25/app/rain-button.test.ts) as a static contract test since the repo has no DOM setup.
